newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: S.African countries to push for Japan ivory deal.
newsitem.headline: S.African countries to push for Japan ivory deal.

text.p: Four southern African countries will lobby the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) next June to sell most of their stockpiled ivory to Japan, a Botswana government official said on Tuesday.

Botswana's director of wildlife, Sedia Modise, said members of the Southern Africa Wildlife Management -- Botswana, Malawi, Zimbabwe and Namibia -- group will also request a resumption in the regulated trade of live elephants and other elephant products.
Modise said no more elephants would be shot and no ivory other than from the stockpiles would be traded.
"Trade in skins, feet, and hair would be only in products generated from recreational hunting. Live animals would only be sold to acceptable destinations, with their tusks protected," he said.
Signatories to the 134-member CITES were due to meet in the Zimbabwean capital Harare in June next year.
The four southern African countries will present proposals to transfer their elephant populations from the convention's Appendix I to Appendix II, under which limited trade is allowed.
Japan has offered to buy the ivory stockpiled by the three countries whilst they have been prevented since 1989 in engaging in any trade in elephant products. No other buyers are in mind.
"Japan has agreed not to re-export the ivory, or products made from it," Modise said. "There is enough demand for ivory in Japan for it to be absorbed locally."

The proposals offer that the trade, envisaged to be in two direct shipments during 1998 and 1999, should be monitored by CITES officials during export and subsequent import. Tusks would be marked and registered.
"Botswana has stockpiled 30 tonnes of ivory since 1989," deputy wildlife director Joseph Matlhare said.
"Not all of it would be for sale. That which is not of Botswana origin -- that confiscated whilst in transit by poachers -- would be held back," he added.
Similarly, Namibia and Zimbabwe would offer only ivory that has originated in their own countries. No figures were given for the amount of ivory stockiled by those countries. Malawi has no stockpile.
Botswana has a growing elephant population, now more than 79,000.
